title: Supplementary qPCR data for expression of genes related to bone metabolism in saliva of patients during early fixed orthodontic treatment
author: Alah Dawood Aldawoody
license_note: figshare article detail endpoint license.name: CC BY 4.0

steps.instruction: In the present prospective clinical study, we investigated changes in the expression levels of the bone remodeling-related genes (RANKL, OPG, ALP, TRAP, RUNX2) in orthodontic patients' saliva in response to the early stages of fixed orthodontic treatment among 24 patients. Saliva samples were collected at baseline (day 0), 24h, 7 days, and 30 days after archwire ligation, and analyzed by means of real time-PCR. Our findings revealed that the level of expression of bone resorption markers (RANKL and TRAP) significantly increased at 24h and were downregulated after 7 day; while the expression of bone formation markers (OPG, ALP and RUNX2) increased at day 7 onwards. At 24h post-ligation, the ratio of RANKL/OPG was higher which means that bone resorption is active, and this level decreased steadily up to day 30, suggesting the dominance of bone formation. In conclusion, analysis of salivary gene expression seems to be a promising method for monitoring the course of bone remodeling during orthodontic tooth movement in a non-invasive way, and might help to make treatment protocol much more personalized.
